Forecast Discussion

Record highs were set across the region, but it takes a few days for all the details to come in on official gauges. Our station’s high was 81, 4 degrees above the old record.

A cold front crosses the mountains this afternoon. Behind it, a strong high pressure area builds from the Plains, and the pressure difference between the two drives the wind tonight and Saturday. The rain is modest -- a few showers this evening, more later tonight, and showers and drizzle Saturday morning that end as the drier air arrives by early afternoon. The cold is the story: Saturday feels like a different season.

The high settles over Virginia and the Carolinas Sunday. Winds ease, skies clear, and both Saturday night and Sunday night bring freezing temperatures to most of the area, with the coldest spots in the valleys.

The high drifts to New England Monday and holds there through midweek, keeping a cool northeast breeze going. At the same time, an upper-level low stalls off the Southeast coast. It stays east of us, but a low like this always deserves a wary eye. It may spread clouds back our way beginning Wednesday, and Thursday runs mostly cloudy. No rain is in the forecast from it at this time.

Temperatures recover slowly through the week. I doubt we will see anything close to Thursday’s heat until next spring.
